articleTitle: Erratum to: Tamagawa Products of Elliptic Curves over Q
A Unified Approach to the Arens Regularity and Related Problems for a Class of Banach Algebras Associated with Locally Compact Groups
abstract: Based on Katznelson–Tzafriri Theorem on power bounded operators, we prove in this paper a theorem, which applies to the most of the classical Banach algebras of harmonic analysis associated with locally compact groups, to deal with the problems when a given Banach algebra A is Arens regular and when A is an ideal in its bidual. In the second part of the paper, we study the topological center of the bidual of a class of Banach algebras with a multiplier bounded approximate identity.

articleTitle: Definable Regularity Lemmas for Nip Hypergraphs
abstract: We present a systematic study of the regularity phenomena for NIP hypergraphs and connections to the theory of (locally) generically stable measures, providing a model-theoretic hypergraph version of the results of Alon-Fischer-Newman and Lovász-Szegedy for graphs of bounded VC-dimension. We also consider the two extremal cases of regularity for stable and distal hypergraphs, improving and generalizing the corresponding results for graphs in the literature. Finally, we consider a related question of the existence of large (approximately) homogeneous definable subsets of NIP hypergraphs and provide some positive results and counterexamples, in particular for graphs definable in the p-adics.

articleTitle: The Space of Traces in Symmetric Monoidal Infinity Categories
abstract: We define a tracelike transformation to be a natural family of conjugation invariant maps <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{x,\mathtt{C}}:\hom_\mathtt{C}(x, x) \to \hom_\mathtt{C}(\unicode{x1D7D9},\unicode{x1D7D9})$</tex> for all dualizable objects x in any symmetric monoidal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty$</tex>-category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathtt{C}$</tex>. This generalizes the trace from linear algebra that assigns a scalar <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Tr}(\,f\,) \in k$</tex> to any endomorphism f : V → V of a finite-dimensional k-vector space. Our main theorem computes the moduli space of tracelike transformations using the one-dimensional cobordism hypothesis with singularities. As a consequence, we show that the trace <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Tr}$</tex> can be uniquely extended to a tracelike transformation up to a contractible space of choices. This allows us to give several model-independent characterizations of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty$</tex>-categorical trace.By restricting the aforementioned notion of tracelike transformations from endomorphisms to automorphisms one can in particular recover a theorem of Toën and Vezzosi. Other examples of tracelike transformations are for instance given by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f \mapsto \operatorname{Tr}(\,f^{\,n})$</tex>. Unlike for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Tr}$</tex>, the relevant connected component of the moduli space is not contractible, but rather equivalent to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$</tex> or BS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> for n = 0. As a result, we obtain a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$</tex>-action on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Tr}(\,f^{\,n})$</tex> as well as a circle action on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Tr}(\operatorname{id}_x)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Pullback of the Normal Module of Ideals with Low Codimension
abstract: The normal module (or sheaf) of an ideal is a celebrated object in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry. In this paper, we prove results about its pullback under the natural projection, focusing on subtle numerical invariants such as, for instance, the reduction number. For certain codimension 2 perfect ideals, we show that the pullback has reduction number two. This is of interest since the determination of this invariant in the context of modules (even for special classes) is a mostly open, difficult problem. The analytic spread is also computed. Finally, for codimension 3 Gorenstein ideals, we determine the depth of the pullback, and we also consider a broader class of ideals provided that the Auslander transpose of the conormal module is almost Cohen–Macaulay.

articleTitle: Tamagawa Products of Elliptic Curves Over ℚ
abstract: We explicitly construct the Dirichlet series <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*}L_{\mathrm{Tam}}(s):=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\frac{P_{\mathrm{Tam}}(m)}{m^s},\end{equation*}$$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\mathrm{Tam}}(m)$</tex> is the proportion of elliptic curves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E/\mathbb{Q}$</tex> in short Weierstrass form with Tamagawa product m. Although there are no <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E/\mathbb{Q}$</tex> with everywhere good reduction, we prove that the proportion with trivial Tamagawa product is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\mathrm{Tam}}(1)={0.5053\dots}$</tex>. As a corollary, we find that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\mathrm{Tam}}(-1)={1.8193\dots}$</tex> is the average Tamagawa product for elliptic curves over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Q}$</tex>. We give an application of these results to canonical and Weil heights.

articleTitle: Gradient Estimates of ω-Minimizers to Double Phase Variational Problems with Variable Exponents
abstract: We are concerned with an optimal regularity for ω-minimizers to double phase variational problems with variable exponents where the associated energy density is allowed to be discontinuous. We identify basic structure assumptions on the density for the absence of Lavrentiev phenomenon and higher integrability. Moreover, we establish a local Calderón–Zygmund theory for such generalized minimizers under minimal regularity requirements regarding such double phase functionals to the frame of Lebesgue spaces with variable exponents.

articleTitle: Transversal Hard Lefschetz Theorem on Transversely Symplectic Foliations
abstract: We study the transversal hard Lefschetz theorem on a transversely symplectic foliation. This article extends the results of transversally symplectic flows (H.K. Pak, “Transversal harmonic theory for transversally symplectic flows”, J. Aust. Math. Soc. 84 (2008), 233–245) to general transversely symplectic foliations.

articleTitle: The Maximum Entropy of a Metric Space
abstract: We define a one-parameter family of entropies, each assigning a real number to any probability measure on a compact metric space (or, more generally, a compact Hausdorff space with a notion of similarity between points). These generalize the Shannon and Rényi entropies of information theory. We prove that on any space X, there is a single probability measure maximizing all these entropies simultaneously. Moreover, all the entropies have the same maximum value: the maximum entropy of X. As X is scaled up, the maximum entropy grows, and its asymptotics determine geometric information about X, including the volume and dimension. And the large-scale limit of the maximizing measure itself provides an answer to the question: what is the canonical measure on a metric space? Primarily, we work not with entropy itself but its exponential, which in its finite form is already in use as a measure of biodiversity. Our main theorem was first proved in the finite case by Leinster and Meckes.

articleTitle: Second Moment Of Dirichlet L-Functions, Character Sums Over Subgroups And Upper Bounds On Relative Class Numbers
abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for the mean-square average of L-functions associated with subgroups of characters of sufficiently large size. Our proof relies on the study of certain character sums <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{A}}(p,d)$</tex> recently introduced by E. Elma, where p ≥ 3 is prime and d ≥ 1 is any odd divisor of p − 1. We obtain an asymptotic formula for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{A}}(p,d),$</tex> which holds true for any odd divisor d of p − 1, thus removing E. Elma's restrictions on the size of d. This answers a question raised in Elma's paper. Our proof relies on both estimates on the frequency of large character sums and techniques from the theory of uniform distribution. As an application, in the range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\leq d\leq\frac{\log p}{3\log\log p}$</tex>, we obtain a significant improvement <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h_{p,d}^- \leq 2(\frac{(1+o(1))p}{24})^{m/4}$</tex> over the trivial bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h_{p,d}^- \ll (\frac{dp}{24} )^{m/4}$</tex> on the relative class numbers of the imaginary number fields of conductor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p\equiv 1\mod{2d}$</tex> and degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m=(p-1)/d$</tex>, where d ≥ 1 is odd.

articleTitle: The Rationality of the Moduli Space of Two-pointed Ineffective Spin Hyperelliptic Curves
abstract: By the geometry of the 3-fold quadric, we show that the coarse moduli space of genus g ineffective spin hyperelliptic curves with two marked points is a rational variety for every g ≥ 2.

articleTitle: On Sums Of Coefficients Of Maass Forms For SL(3, ℤ)
abstract: Let f be a Maass form for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SL(3,{\mathbb{Z}})$</tex> with coefficients A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>(m, n). The aim of this paper is to study the asymptotic behaviour of the sum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum_{m\leqslant x,n\leqslant y}|A_f(m,n)|^2$</tex> and some other related sums.

articleTitle: Well-Posedness and Stability of a Generalized Micropolar Thermoelastic Body With Infinite Memory
abstract: We study in this paper the well-posedness and stability of a linear system of a thermoelastic Cosserat medium with infinite memory, where the Cosserat medium is a continuum in which each point has the degrees of freedom of a rigid body.

articleTitle: Surjective Homomorphisms from Algebras of Operators on Long Sequence Spaces are Automatically Injective
abstract: We study automatic injectivity of surjective algebra homomorphisms from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{B}(X)$</tex>, the algebra of (bounded, linear) operators on X, to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{B}(Y)$</tex>, where X is one of the following long sequence spaces: c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(λ), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell_{\infty}^c(\lambda)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell_p(\lambda)$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \leqslant p \lt \infty$</tex>) and Y is arbitrary. En route to the proof that these spaces do indeed enjoy such a property, we classify two-sided ideals of the algebra of operators of any of the aforementioned Banach spaces that are closed with respect to the ‘sequential strong operator topology’.

A linear equation with coefficients in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_q$</tex> is common if the number of monochromatic solutions in any two-coloring of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_q^{\,n}$</tex> is asymptotically (as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \to \infty$</tex>) at least the number expected in a random two-coloring. The linear equation is Sidorenko if the number of solutions in any dense subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_q^{\,n}$</tex> is asymptotically at least the number expected in a random set of the same density. In this paper, we characterize those linear equations which are common, and those which are Sidorenko. The main novelty is a construction based on choosing random Fourier coefficients that shows that certain linear equations do not have these properties. This solves problems posed in a paper of Saad and Wolf.

We give a new and conceptually straightforward proof of the well-known presentation for the Temperley–Lieb algebra, via an alternative new presentation. Our method involves twisted semigroup algebras, and we make use of two apparently new submonoids of the Temperley–Lieb monoid.

We generalize a Theorem of Ricci and count Gaussian primes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{p}$</tex> with short interval restrictions on both the norm and the argument of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{p}$</tex>. We follow Heath-Brown's method for counting rational primes in short intervals.
